chunks: Al-Washa' narrated from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abu Khadeeja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I had a daughter, and I raised her until she reached maturity. I dressed her in new clothes and adorned her with jewelry, then I brought her to a well and pushed her into its depths. The last thing I heard from her was her saying, 'O father!' So what is the expiation for that?'

He (peace be upon him and his family) asked, 'Do you have a living mother?' He said, 'No.' He asked, 'Do you have a living maternal aunt?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So be righteous to her, for she is in the position of the mother. It will be an expiation for you for what you did.'

Abu Khadeeja said, 'So I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When was this?'' He said, 'It was in the period of Ignorance (pre-Islamic era), and they used to kill their daughters out of fear that they would be captured as captives and give birth among other people.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْأُمِّ: In the position/status of the mother
key_terms.كَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or atonement for a sin or deed

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a daughter in Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the pre-Islamic practice of female infanticide, where the Prophet prescribed kindness to the maternal aunt as expiation, establishing her status as a secondary mother figure in Shia jurisprudence. The context clarifies that this specific ruling addressed the fear of daughters being captured and enslaved by rival tribes, a unique socio-historical concern of the Jahiliyyah period. It underscores the enduring value of maintaining family ties (silat al-rahim) as a means of spiritual purification.

en.hubeali:
Al Washha, from Ahmad Bin Aiz, from Abu Khadeeja, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘There was a daughter born unto me, and I nourished her until when she became an adult, so I put some new clothes on her and some ornaments, then went with her to a well and pushed her into its middle (to kill her), and the last of what I heard from her was that she was saying, ‘O father ! So what is the expiation of that?’

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Is there a mother for you, alive?’ He said, ‘No’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘So for you there is a maternal aunt, alive?’ He said, ‘Yes’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘So be righteous with her, for she is at the status of the mother. It would expiate you from what you did’.

Abu Khadeeja (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘When was this?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘During the pre-Islamic period, and they used to kill the daughters fearing that they would be made captives, so they would give birth among other people’.
en.sarwar: 18. Al-Washsha’ has narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Ai’z from abu Khadijah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once a man came to the Holy Prophet and said, ‘I had a daughter and I brought her up until she became an adult. I then dressed her up in beautiful clothes, took her to the well and threw her therein to her death and the last thing I heard from her was; O father! What is the expiation for it?’

The Messenger of Allah asked, ‘Do you have a living mother?’ He said, ‘No, I do not.’ The Messenger of Allah asked, ‘Do you have a living maternal aunt?’ He said, ‘Yes, I do.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Be kind to her; she is like a mother, this will serve as expiation for what you have done.’

Abu Khadijah has said, ‘I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘When was this?’ The Imam said, ‘It was in the time of Jahiliyah (age of darkness). They would kill the girls for fear of being taken captive and giving birth to other people.’”
